name: Green politics
summary: Green politics seeks an ecologically sustainable society built on ecological wisdom, social justice, grassroots democracy and nonviolence. It rejects growth for its own sake, opposes nuclear power, favours decentralised participatory democracy and generous public welfare, and distrusts corporate power and free trade. Views on markets range from eco-socialist to eco-capitalist, but the mainstream backs a regulated mixed economy.
scope: The mainstream of the global Green party family, taken from Wikipedia's overview, the Global Greens Charter and the US Green Party platform, which is more eco-socialist than many European parties. Green conservatives, green liberals and deep-ecology radicals are noted as variants but not the basis. Positions not stated by the sources are inferred at low confidence.

sources.usedFor: Six principles: ecological wisdom, social justice, participatory democracy, nonviolence, sustainability, respect for diversity.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The US Green platform calls for single-payer care and says health care is a right, not a privilege.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Greens distrust unregulated capitalism and want ecological limits and public direction, while accepting private firms and co-ops within a mixed economy.

public-ownership.rationale: The platform envisions a mixed economy with municipalization and publicly owned enterprise, and prefers public ownership and planning in clean energy.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The platform proposes an annual wealth tax, restored estate tax and equal taxation of unearned income.

unions-good.rationale: The platform calls for strictly enforcing and expanding workers' rights to organize, as part of social justice.

property-fundamental.rationale: Greens subordinate property to ecological and social limits, favouring corporate charters with social duties and community-owned land.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The platform would curb corporate power, end corporate personhood and revoke charters of repeat law-breakers.

cut-welfare.rationale: The platform opposes workfare and time limits and calls for a strong safety net and basic income.

worker-ownership.rationale: It supports incentives for worker and consumer co-ops and stakeholder ownership, though alongside private and public firms.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The platform calls for repealing the PATRIOT Act and ending warrantless wiretaps and bulk data collection.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Greens call for ending the war on drugs and decriminalizing victimless offences; full commercial legalisation is less uniformly stated.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: US Greens oppose censorship while European parties often back hate-speech laws, and the sources do not settle it.

strong-leader.rationale: Grassroots democracy and decentralized, consensus decision-making are core pillars, which rules out bypassing checks.

state-harmful.rationale: Greens want better, more democratic government and public institutions, not abolition of the state.

empower-police-military.rationale: The platform would halve the defense budget and remove police from schools.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The platform supports decriminalizing consensual adult sex work while opposing trafficking.

decide-locally.rationale: Local control, bioregional democracy and bottom-up parties are central, with states and cities free to set stricter standards.

rehabilitation.rationale: The platform favours restorative justice and opposes long sentences for victimless crimes and for-profit detention.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The platform supports LGBTQIA rights, including recognition of same-sex marriages and civil unions.

abortion-legal.rationale: The platform calls women's right to control their bodies non-negotiable and supports legal, funded abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: The platform opposes religiously based public school curricula.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: It supports affirmative action and reparations, including a reparations trust fund.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Greens protect local and indigenous cultures and diversity but are not nationalist, so there is no clear position on the national culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Greens call for fundamental transformation of the economy and energy system, though they work through elections and institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The platform seeks a path to citizenship and opposes the border wall, E-Verify and Title 42 expulsions.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: It wants disputes taken to the UN and the ICC but replaced WTO, IMF and World Bank with democratic bodies.

free-trade.rationale: The platform opposes free trade that puts corporate interests above national law and backs fair trade.

nation-first.rationale: Greens stress global solidarity, international law and climate debt, not putting national interest above cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The platform allows force only to repel an actual attack and opposes preemptive war, though it backs ICC and UN processes.

limit-growth.rationale: The platform states unlimited growth on a finite planet cannot be sustained and favours a steady-state economy.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: It calls for an Ecosocialist Green New Deal reaching zero emissions in a decade.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Greens apply the precautionary principle to technology and place the burden of proof on proponents.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Greens mostly oppose nuclear power; the US platform calls for retiring reactors and a moratorium.

revolution-justified.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): the old wording asked whether revolution is sometimes justified, and this disagreement rested on a preference for reform or lawful means, which doesn't say revolution is never justified.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nonviolence is one of the four pillars, so adherents generally favour change through democratic and nonviolent means.

experts-over-public.rationale: Participatory and deliberative democracy are core values, though Greens also rely on scientific evidence.

central-planning.rationale: Ecosocialist Greens favour planning in energy, but the platform stresses local, mixed and co-op economy, and adherents differ.

socialized-markets.rationale: The platform envisions markets with co-ops, public enterprises and small business rather than investor-owned corporations.

land-value-tax.rationale: The platform supports land value taxation and a green tax shift, though not as replacing most other taxes.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The platform would restore the estate tax as part of fairer taxation.

basic-income.rationale: The platform calls for an unconditional universal basic income for every adult.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Greens favour local production and a carbon border fee but oppose free trade rather than endorse protectionism as such.

state-directs-investment.rationale: It prefers public investment and planning over private subsidies for a green transition.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The platform backs small business, small farms, co-ops and community ownership against corporate concentration.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Not a Green aim; the platform seeks living wages and a shorter work week, not abolition of wage labor.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The platform wants a public monetary authority, not market-run money.

one-party-rule.rationale: Grassroots democracy and proportional representation are foundational.

democracy-best.rationale: Participatory democracy is one of the Global Greens' six principles.

direct-votes.rationale: The platform supports initiative, referendum and recall at all levels.

workers-councils.rationale: Greens prize grassroots participation but pursue it through elected assemblies, so councils replacing parliaments is not their model.

right-to-secede.rationale: Wikipedia notes bioregional democracy and urban secession and the platform backs self-determination, but this is not a general principle.

natural-rulers.rationale: Equality and grassroots democracy contradict natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Nonviolence is a core pillar, though adherents may allow self-defence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Peace is a core value and the platform seeks deep military cuts.

separate-church-state.rationale: The platform opposes religious curricula in public schools.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Greens want public provision, curbs on corporate power and demilitarized democratic security.

military-superiority.rationale: The platform seeks to halve defense spending and close foreign bases.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Respect for diversity is a Global Greens principle.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Eco-socialists stress class but the Green mainstream is not Marxist in its theory of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The platform seeks economic equality through wealth taxes and basic income, but the stated aim is justice and a livable income.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The platform recognizes tribal sovereignty and treaty obligations and supports UNDRIP.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The platform asserts a climate and ecological debt to the Global South and calls for debt cancellation.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Greens criticise consumerism and stress ecological wisdom and social justice over self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Greens stress rights and responsibility to nature, but not duties to the community above rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Ecological wisdom and rights of nature are central; the platform says humans owe moral responsibility to other species.

limit-population.rationale: The platform supports efforts to slow population growth through living standards, food security and family planning.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Greens criticise productivism but the mainstream seeks reform, not rejection of industrial society.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The precautionary principle and moratoria on GMOs point against speeding up technological change.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The platform says Fourth Amendment privacy extends online and seeks privacy-protecting internet structures.

restore-past-order.rationale: Greens seek a forward-looking transformation, generally left-leaning and progressive.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Greens claim to go beyond left and right but hold firm value commitments, so views are split.

direct-action.rationale: Greens combine party-building with support for nonviolent protest, so both are accepted.

means-match-ends.rationale: Nonviolence and grassroots democracy are meant to be practiced in the way the movement works.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Mainstream Greens seek sustainable modern society with regenerative agriculture.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The platform favours a basic income and priority to basic needs but not an end to work-based pay.

production-for-use.rationale: Greens reject growth for its own sake and favour meeting needs locally, but not abolition of profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Eco-socialist strands endorse this and eco-capitalist ones do not.

collective-farming.rationale: The platform favours small and medium farms and community-owned farmland rather than compulsory collectivization.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Some Greens blame capitalism for ecological harm and war, but this is not a core claim.

taxation-theft.rationale: The platform proposes new taxes on wealth, carbon and land value.

harm-principle.rationale: Greens defend personal liberties on drugs and sex work but also regulate heavily for ecological and health reasons.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The platform recognizes tribal sovereignty and collective rights of indigenous peoples.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Democratic participation is a pillar; exit is not offered as an alternative.

state-as-business.rationale: Greens reject market logic for government and want public enterprise and democratic accountability.

positive-liberty.rationale: The platform's right to health care, livable income and basic income presumes material means for freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: The platform stresses corporate and money power over media, not academia-media rule.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Greens affirm equality and oppose racial discrimination.

organic-representation.rationale: The platform seeks proportional representation of parties, not corporate bodies replacing parties.

total-state.rationale: Contradicts grassroots democracy and civil liberties.

national-rebirth.rationale: Greens are internationalist and progressive, not a rebirth of the nation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The platform opposes preemptive war and covert destabilization.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Inconsistent with democracy and the rule of law.

bound-labor.rationale: Contradicts social justice and workers' rights.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Ecofeminist and critical strands accept this but Greens also rely on science.

universal-morality.rationale: Global Greens adopt shared universal values yet respect diversity, so the sources do not settle it.

single-common-good.rationale: Greens stress pluralism and respect for diversity, though ecological wisdom is a shared aim.

workplace-democracy.rationale: It supports democratic co-ops, and worker and management control of pension funds.

school-vouchers.rationale: The platform opposes vouchers and privatization of public education.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The platform opposes austerity and not deficits as such, though it also lists national debt reform.

economic-freedom.rationale: Greens favour public and democratic control of the economy, though they back political freedoms strongly.

national-self-determination.rationale: The platform backs self-determination for Puerto Rico and Kurds.

force-without-un.rationale: The platform says force is legitimate only to repel attack and wants disputes taken to the UN.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Greens draw on science but many value spiritual and non-rational ecological wisdom.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The platform opposes workfare and time limits on benefits.

class-collaboration.rationale: Greens back co-ops and stakeholder ownership but also curb corporate power.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Greens stress preservation, community and cultural diversity.

dominated-front.rationale: The platform calls for global solidarity and debt cancellation but not blocs against Western powers.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The platform pushes gender equality and post-patriarchal values.

ban-interest.rationale: The platform caps consumer interest rates but does not prohibit lending at interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The platform supports ending racial discrimination and profiling.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Eco-socialists lean that way but mainstream Greens see the state as reformable.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The platform calls for halting new fossil fuel infrastructure and ending subsidies.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The platform supports bilingualism and the Global Greens respect diversity.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim at odds with the platform's pro-immigrant stance.

proportional-representation.rationale: The platform supports proportional voting for legislatures at all levels.

national-mission.rationale: The platform favours peaceful dispute resolution and ending covert interference abroad.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Post-patriarchal values and ecofeminism are part of green thought.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Greens reject corporate money and seek public financing, implying distrust of established elites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Contradicts the platform's equal rights and reproductive freedom.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The platform calls for health care, income and extensive regulation.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The platform seeks equal rights and social justice, and respect for diversity is a charter principle.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not a Green question, since Greens do not hold a doctrine of socialism in one country.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: The platform seeks to phase out factory farming and encourages plant-based diets but not a ban.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The platform opposes religiously based curricula in public schools.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Participatory democracy underpins legitimacy for Greens.

trade-surplus.rationale: Greens favour local production and fair trade, not export drives.

population-transfer.rationale: Contradicts rights and respect for diversity.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Greens emphasize cooperation and criticize consumerism and growth.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The platform stresses free speech but Green parties in Europe often back such protection.

separated-powers.rationale: Greens favour checks and balances and distributed power.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The platform stresses ending poverty and a strong safety net.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The platform seeks to expand workers' rights to organize.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The platform says overpopulation largely results from poverty, not the reverse.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Respect for diversity is a Global Greens principle.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The platform backs citizens' assemblies but not lottery in place of election.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The platform opposes curtailing civil rights in the name of security.

party-controls-media.rationale: The platform opposes censorship and calls for media reform.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The platform seeks pathways to citizenship for undocumented immigrants.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Greens emphasize consensus and grassroots autonomy over binding discipline.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Greens oppose war but do not hold a doctrine of working for defeat.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The platform opposes censorship in arts, media and internet.

recall-officials.rationale: The platform supports recall at all levels.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Nulled: the statement now asks only about permanent military alliances (the troops half moved to troops-home-from-abroad, 2026-11-10), and these sources speak to closing foreign bases and bringing troops home, not alliances (the platform names no alliance, pact or bloc).

reviewHistory.rationale: The platform would close most foreign bases and cut the military.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The platform supports public housing and tenant protections.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Greens value local and agrarian life but also sustainable cities.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Respect for diversity is a charter principle.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The platform supports age-appropriate education on gender, sexuality and safer sex.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The platform opposes religiously based curricula.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The platform seeks inclusive citizenship pathways.

minority-language-support.rationale: The platform supports national bilingualism and protection of languages.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The platform urges the IMF and World Bank to end recipient nations' debts.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The platform backs deliberative bodies and citizen assemblies.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Greens reject growth as a goal and defend civil liberties.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The platform supports NGO development and health funding and a climate debt.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The platform seeks abolition of nuclear weapons.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The platform wants public monetary authority under democratic control.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The platform favours community ownership and ecological limits on property.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The platform ties debt and trade reform to development of poorer nations.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Greens treat the precautionary principle as a core rule for technology and environment, placing the burden of proof on proponents.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Greens have no stated view on the office; in parliamentary republics Green parties accept a ceremonial unifying president, so this is an inference.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on general self-government, separate laws or no stated position, not on keeping a distinct economic system, and the statement now asks only whether a region joining a larger state should be free to keep its economic system.

reviewHistory.rationale: Decentralisation and grassroots democracy are core Green principles, which support regional autonomy with its own arrangements.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Participatory democracy and a secular, egalitarian outlook leave no place for a sacred or divinely descended ruler.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The platform backs progressive taxation that shifts the burden onto high incomes and corporations, the opposite of a flat rate.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The platform's emphasis on civil liberties, accountability and democratic control rules out rulers who stand above the law.

leader-cult.rationale: Grassroots democracy and non-hierarchical organisation are core principles, so glorifying a leader is rejected.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Charter makes freedom and respect for diversity core values and the US platform backs freedom of conscience.

women-must-cover.rationale: The Charter's equality and freedom principles and the platform's social justice section oppose such dress mandates.

common-currency.rationale: Green parties are split, with pro-euro parties in Europe and critics of monetary union backed by the US platform's stress on local economies.

ban-cartels.rationale: The platform opposes corporate concentration and seeks to strengthen antitrust and break up monopolies.

no-bailouts.rationale: The US Greens opposed bank bailouts and favour public banking, though the platform's wording on this was not checked in detail.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The platform seeks fair trade and trade rules that put labor and environmental protection first.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Nonviolence is a core Global Greens principle and the platform backs peaceful means.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Greens hold to nonviolence, self-determination and respect for diversity, which rules out rule over other peoples as tutelage.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The US platform supports affirmative action and remedies for racial discrimination.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Greens oppose imperialism and favour global justice, so influence from past empire is not a claim they endorse.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The platform calls for strong anti-discrimination laws in work, housing and services.

elective-rulers.rationale: Grassroots democracy is a pillar and the platform wants elected, accountable government; a hereditary ruler is inconsistent with it.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The Green platform calls cruelty to animals repugnant and seeks to end factory farming and animal testing.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Many Greens favour vegetarianism and want to phase out animal testing and factory farming, so humane use alone is not enough, though some strands accept it.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Green politics is built on grassroots participation and active citizenship, so withdrawal from public life runs against it.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Greens criticise corporate influence over politics and media but do not use a hegemony account; adherents are split on how power is kept.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The platform criticises free trade and global financial institutions as exploiting poorer countries and calls for fair trade and debt cancellation.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Greens are split between removing monuments to oppressors and preserving history in context.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The platform opposes domestic violence and seeks services for all victims, but does not take a position on the symmetry claim.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Greens are rooted in nonviolence and peace politics, and favour demilitarisation and civilian control of the military.

paid-care-work.rationale: The platform calls for valuing unpaid care and domestic work and for support such as paid family leave and a guaranteed income.

filial-duty.rationale: Greens stress community and care, but family duty is not a platform item and adherents split between traditional and individual-choice views.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Greens favour land trusts and common stewardship, but mainstream parties do not call for ending private ownership; adherents are split.

single-official-language.rationale: The Global Greens Charter includes respect for diversity, which runs against imposing one language on public life.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Greens reject growth for its own sake and call for lower consumption and less waste.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Nonviolence is a core Green principle and the platform opposes military intervention and covert war.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Nonviolence and respect for self-determination are core Green principles, so force against an ally is rejected.

corporate-influence.rationale: The Green platform calls for publicly financed elections and limits on corporate lobbying and power.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Greens favour national self-determination but also open civil society; no stated position on restricting foreign funding.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Greens favour support for families and child care, but reject population growth targets and incentive-driven pronatalism.

job-guarantee.rationale: The US Green platform backs a federal job guarantee as employer of last resort.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Greens' commitment to social justice and anti-discrimination rejects ethnic conspiracy theories.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Democracy platform stresses transparency and open government.

local-production.rationale: Local, sustainable production and community-based economies are core Green positions.

religious-nation.rationale: Greens favour secular, pluralist politics and reject defining the nation by religion.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on accepting or rejecting common ownership of production, or on private property in general, and the statement now asks only whether personal belongings should stay private where production is held in common.

reviewHistory.rationale: The platform backs a regulated mixed economy with cooperatives, not common ownership of all means of production.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Greens reject growth for its own sake and blame corporate capitalism for ecological and social harm.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The Global Greens Charter and US platform call for human rights and equal rights, including for LGBT people.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Green platform calls for civil liberties, free expression and democratic participation, so suppressing opposition is rejected.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The platform supports separation of church and state and religious freedom.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Global Greens Charter and US platform oppose imperialism and economic domination of other countries.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Nonviolence and grassroots democracy are core principles, so removing rulers by force is rejected.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Grassroots democracy is one of the four pillars and the Global Greens Charter calls for participatory democracy in communities and workplaces.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The US platform links racial, gender and economic justice together, and the Charter holds social justice as a pillar.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The US Green platform calls for full equal rights regardless of gender identity.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Greens describe themselves as 'neither left nor right but ahead', combining ideas from both, though US Greens place themselves on the left.

alienated-labor.rationale: The platform criticises corporate capitalism and exploitation of workers, but it does not use alienation theory explicitly.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Grassroots democracy and popular sovereignty are pillars of Green politics, so authority from God is rejected.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The platform supports workers' rights and ending forced arbitration in employment disputes.

social-market-economy.rationale: The platform backs a regulated mixed economy with strong social protections and anti-monopoly rules, rejecting laissez-faire.

rich-first.rationale: Social justice and ending inequality are core, so letting some grow rich first is rejected.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The US platform opposes military alliances and interventions and promotes nonviolence and diplomacy.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Greens stress grassroots democracy and accountability, which is incompatible with hereditary office.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The Green Party platform criticises IMF and World Bank structural adjustment and corporate-led globalisation, and favours debt relief for poor countries.

property-franchise.rationale: Greens stand for universal participation and social justice; the platform backs expanded voting rights and rejects wealth-based exclusion.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is one strand of Green thought and platforms pair ecology with gender equality, but the link is not a position of the whole family.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The US Green platform attacks corporate concentration of media and money in politics and calls for public-interest media and campaign finance reform.

racial-franchise.rationale: Greens strongly oppose racial discrimination and champion equality and anti-racism.

online-participation.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale is about online deliberation, consultation or political participation in general, not voting, and the statement now asks whether citizens should have the option to vote online in public elections.

reviewHistory.rationale: Participatory and direct democracy are core Green values and the platform supports using technology to widen citizen involvement, though with caution about digital divides.

open-government-data.rationale: Green commitments to transparency, accountability and participatory democracy support open publication of decision records.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Greens defend freedom of religion and belief and oppose discrimination on religion.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Targeting minority-owned shops is discrimination that the platform and charter condemn, though Greens do back consumer boycotts of corporations.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Grassroots, participatory democracy is a core Green pillar and many Green parties back deliberative citizens' assemblies, though the platform text cited does not name sortition.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Green Party platform criticises corporate concentration of wealth and power and calls for economic justice and democratic control of the economy.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The Green Party platform in social justice opposes discrimination based on sexual orientation, so open service would be accepted.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The Green platform calls for robust public programs and a strong welfare state rather than reliance on private charity.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The Green Party platform calls for gender equality and equal treatment in all institutions, and the Global Greens Charter affirms equality of women.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Green platform and Global Greens Charter affirm gender equality, which covers equal authority in marriage.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The grassroots-democracy pillar extends participation to residents, and the US platform backs voting rights for non-citizen residents locally.

rent-control.rationale: The social justice platform treats housing as a right and backs tenant protections and rent regulation.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Global Greens Charter makes nonviolence a core principle, which excludes drilled national-service youth organisations.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Opposition to nuclear power and weapons is a defining Green position, and the platform calls for nuclear disarmament.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The platform calls for closing foreign bases and ending military interventionism, as part of nonviolence.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The economic justice platform wants a living wage and workers' ownership, and criticises unearned wealth and corporate power.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Nonviolence is a core principle, but the charter does not say whether defensive killing is always wrong, and adherents divide.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Charter is internationalist and global in outlook, and Greens distrust nationalist narratives of ancient continuity.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Greens are mostly secular and pluralist; some spiritual ecology exists but politics is not framed as a battle of good and evil.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The social justice platform opposes discrimination and minority exclusion, so reserving economic life for a majority is rejected.

independent-unions.rationale: The platform backs workers' rights to organise and bargain; independence from state and party follows from its grassroots, anti-corporatist outlook.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Greens are split between eco-socialists and mixed-economy reformers, and the platform does not make workers' political power a test of socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The platform favours public or community control of utilities and essential services over privatisation.

gm-crops.rationale: The platform calls for restrictions on genetically engineered crops under the precautionary principle.

dense-cities.rationale: Green platforms oppose sprawl and favour compact, transit-oriented development.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Nonviolence is one of the Global Greens' core principles, and the platform opposes wars of aggression.

free-public-college.rationale: The US Green platform backs free public higher education as part of its social justice and economic justice planks; European Greens broadly agree.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Green politics favours ecological taxes and polluter-pays rules, shifting taxes from labour to pollution and resource use.

future-generations.rationale: Sustainability for coming generations is a core principle of the Global Greens Charter and of Green politics generally.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on women's distinct roles, giving their values more weight, a claim about innate nature or no stated position, and the statement now asks only whether women tend to be more compassionate than men.

reviewHistory.rationale: The platform stresses women's equality and participation and a feminist strand runs through Green thought, but it says less about women bringing distinct values.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on women's distinct roles, giving their values more weight, a claim about innate nature or no stated position, and the statement now asks only whether women tend to be more compassionate than men.

arms-reduction.rationale: Nonviolence and disarmament are one of the core Green pillars, and the platform calls for deep cuts to military spending.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The Charter and platform commit to democratic transparency and accountability in international affairs.

capital-controls.rationale: Greens split between wanting limits on footloose capital and supporting open borders for finance; sources do not settle it.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The Green platform on social justice supports workers' rights to organise and bargain collectively.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The Global Greens Charter calls for fair trade, debt relief and reform of the international economic rules for poorer countries.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Greens favour nonviolence and grassroots democracy through electoral and institutional reform, not smashing the existing state.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Greens are split: green economists favour natural-capital accounting while deep-ecology and eco-socialist strands reject pricing nature.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Greens oppose nuclear arms; the US platform and the Global Greens Charter's nonviolence principle point to disarmament.

ban-fgm.rationale: The Global Greens Charter's social justice and human rights principles support banning harmful practices against women.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The platform and the Global Greens Charter commit to gender equality and equal legal rights for women.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Greens favour holding polluters to account, but the platform's emphasis on regulation and public agencies conflicts with the statement's rejection of agency regulation.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Ecological wisdom is the first Green principle and the platform subordinates growth and many freedoms of the market to sustainability, though Greens also stress civil liberties.

voter-id.rationale: The platform on democracy stresses expanding ballot access and opposing voter suppression.

women-suffrage.rationale: The platform's social-justice section supports full equality for women, including political participation.

race-social-construct.rationale: The platform's social-justice section opposes racism and treats race as a social category rather than a biological one.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The platform supports gender equality and public institutions to advance it.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The platform favours commons, community and public stewardship of land and resources over absolute private first-claim ownership.

indirect-election.rationale: The platform champions grassroots democracy and direct participation, including instant-runoff voting, over indirect selection.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The Charter and platform back decentralisation and the self-determination of Indigenous and minority peoples.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Participatory democracy and self-determination in the platform support letting inhabitants vote on their status.

simple-living.rationale: Green ecology calls for lower consumption and voluntary simplicity, reduced needs and local self-reliance.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The US Green platform opposes the drug war and the death penalty and demands due process.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The US Green platform backs taxing resource use and pollution and treating nature as a commons, though it does not state it as an equal-ownership principle.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The platform backs universal programmes such as single-payer care and a guaranteed income, not means-tested targeting.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The platform stresses grassroots democracy and strong parties and groups, so bypassing them is opposed.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The platform opposes corporate subsidies and privileges for connected firms.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The platform stresses women's equality and reproductive and family autonomy.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Green platforms hold that fair distribution is judged by equality and need, not just by how wealth was acquired.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The US Green platform calls for a tax on financial transactions and speculation.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The Green platform treats racism as a continuing structural barrier and calls for measures against it.

multipolar-world.rationale: Greens stress global cooperation and strengthened international institutions rather than a balance among powers; the question does not map cleanly.

material-over-identity.rationale: The Green platform gives equal weight to social justice and identity-based rights alongside economic demands.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Greens favour democratic, decentralised and pluralist politics and reject single-party rule.

troops-home-from-abroad.rationale: The Green Party US platform urges phasing out all foreign bases not under a U.N. peacekeeping resolution and bringing home troops stationed abroad, except embassy guards.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: The platform opposes workfare and time limits and calls for a strong safety net and basic income. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: Greens oppose imperialism and favour global justice, so influence from past empire is not a claim they endorse. (Carried over from former-empire-influence, "A country should cultivate political and cultural influence in regions once ruled by its predecessor empire.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Governments should act to prevent environmental harm even when the science is not yet conclusive.
missingStatements.rationale: Greens treat the precautionary principle as a core rule for technology and environment, placing the burden of proof on proponents.

missingStatements.text: A country's success should be measured by wellbeing and sustainability rather than by GDP.
missingStatements.rationale: The platform rejects GDP growth as the main goal and calls for new measures of economic health.

missingStatements.text: Animals should have legal protections against cruelty, including limits on factory farming.
missingStatements.rationale: The platform calls cruelty to animals repugnant and seeks to phase out factory farming and animal testing.
missingStatements.declined: Animal welfare is a secondary plank and not distinctive enough to justify a bank statement every audit must answer.

notes: Strands differ: eco-socialists favour public ownership and planning, eco-capitalists a regulated market, and some parties (e.g. Finland) accept nuclear power. The US platform is more left-wing than several European Green parties.
